title: Chapter 54
content:
Throughout the drive, Kang Il-hyun kept his gaze fixed outside the window.

It was his first venture out of a sterile hospital room in nearly a week. Lowering the tinted glass, a wave of muggy, midsummer heat rushed into the cabin. Despite the wind whipping his dark hair into complete disarray, he leaned his cheek against the glass like a curious boy, watching the bustling pedestrians drift past.

After a long while, he rolled the window up and rested his head back against the leather seat.

Every slight bump in the asphalt sent a jolt of sharp, throbbing agony through his bandaged legs, pulling an involuntary grimace to his face. Hearing the stifled intake of breath, Park Tae-soo glanced worriedly through the rearview mirror. Defying the head surgeon's direct orders to make an appearance at the board meeting had cost him dearly; being entirely stripped of his mobility was proving to be a grueling inconvenience.

"Are you holding up, Director?"

"It's bearable."

"My deepest apologies. This failure lies entirely with me."

Ever since the shooting, Tae-soo had taken to carrying a burden of relentless, uncharacteristic guilt.

Il-hyun let out a quiet, amused scoff. "How were you supposed to intercept a high-velocity round fired from seventeen floors up? What are you, Superman?"

The quip triggered a sudden, vivid memory of a conversation with Lee Ja-kyeong. The kid had spotted a reflection on a sniper's objective lens, tackling Il-hyun to the floor to dodge a round—only to confess later that he hadn't reacted to the bullet itself, but the glint of sunlight on glass.

Since the inauguration, Il-hyun's network had turned the city upside down, yet the boy had evaporated into thin air without leaving a single trace.

He's long gone. Already across the border.

"I took him far too lightly," Il-hyun muttered aloud with a bitter, incredulous smirk.

After Ja-kyeong’s escape, a military-grade audio transmitter had been discovered tucked beneath the rear seat cushions of the sedan he'd ridden in. The kid had known the contract called for his execution the moment the trigger was pulled. Belatedly, Il-hyun had to concede: he had drastically underestimated his little stray cat.

The bitter taste lingered in his mouth. If everything had gone to plan... would I have actually put a bullet through his head? Why had he hesitated on the morning of the ceremony? Why had he countermanded the kill order at the eleventh hour?

Before the thoughts could untangle, his private line buzzed.

The caller ID displayed Kang Yu-jung. She had attended the shareholder assembly under duress, and watching her brother terrorize the board from a wheelchair had left her wearing a face that screamed she wanted nothing more than to smack him across the skull.

He brought the receiver to his ear. "Did you arrive?"

[Still in transit.]

[Congratulations,] Yu-jung said, her tone dry. [The motion for your dismissal was overwhelmingly rejected. You managed to avoid the unemployment line.]

Il-hyun chuckled softly. "As expected. The board simply recognizes my unmatched executive talent."

A heavy, exasperated sigh came over the line. [They recognized that they didn't want to be butchered and fed to the hounds.]

Il-hyun arched a brow. "Do people actually take such jokes seriously?"

Yu-jung told him she was far too drained to indulge his banter, reminding him to return straight to the clinic before hanging up. They had relocated him to a secure, private medical facility, where Yu-jung intended to stay by his side for the immediate future. Sharing living quarters with an overbearing older sister was hardly his preference, but her stubborn resolve left zero room for argument.

Ending the call, Tae-soo caught his eye in the mirror. "Congratulations, Director."

Il-hyun offered a faint, humorless smile, turning his gaze back to the river. Is this truly something to celebrate?Remembering the terrified, treacherous faces of the board members who had salivated at the prospect of his downfall, he made a silent vow to systematically purge every single one of them from Haewon Group with his own hands.

As for Chairman Kang—so long as the old man remained blind to what cards Il-hyun held, he wouldn't dare make another overt move. Having botched the assassination, the patriarch would scurry into hiding like a wounded animal.

It was almost comical: a father living in visceral terror of his own flesh and blood. Il-hyun had recognized that look for years—the lavish public praise masking a paranoid dread that viewed him as nothing more than a rabid monster.

"Tae-soo."

"Yes, Director."

"Courier the surveillance footage Ja-kyeong recorded straight to the Chairman's desk. Keep his mind occupied so he doesn't cook up any fresh ideas."

"Understood, sir."

Outside, a private yacht drifted lazily along the Han River.

Inevitably, his mind drifted back to the assassin. Did he board a vessel like that? If so, where did he run?

He had considered hunting down every broker and handler connected to the network, subjecting them to systematic torture until they gave up the boy's coordinates. But in the end, he decided against it. Let the prey believe the waters were safe; the moment the little creature felt secure, it would inevitably poke its head out of the shadows.

Run as far as you like.

Savor every drop of your precious freedom, little cat. Because the moment I drag you back into the light, I will make sure you understand the catastrophic weight of what you've done.

The sheer anticipation sent a dark, euphoric rush tingling through his veins. Unable to contain the restless heat in his chest, Il-hyun cracked the window open and sparked a fresh cigarette—the surgeon's strict prohibitions be damned.
Buried deep beneath a plush duvet, curled into a lazy ball, Jakyeong’s morning slumber was gently broken by low, melodic chatter outside.

He blinked the sleep from his eyes, gazing around the sunlit villa. Wang Han was nowhere in sight. Pulling on a loose shirt and running a hand through his tousled hair, Jakyeong padded downstairs and stepped onto the sun-drenched terrace.

A light dawn rain had left the manicured lawn glistening with fresh dew, filling the morning air with a crisp, tropical sweetness.

Stretching his arms overhead, he drew a deep, luxurious breath through his nose, only to catch the mouth-watering aroma of spiced meats searing over an open flame.

Over by the patio grill, Wang Han was already enjoying a chilled beer, turning skewers of marinated lamb alongside two Russian women from the adjacent rental villa.

The sisters, Rita and Sasha, had rented the neighboring estate for the summer season. Over the past few weeks, they had struck up an easy, neighborly friendship with Wang Han, dropping by frequently for meals. Rita, the elder sister, made zero effort to conceal her obvious affection for the sharp-dressed operative.

Following the hit on Kang Il-hyun, Jakyeong, Wang Han, and Wang Ryun had cycled through multiple safehouses across Southeast Asia and the Mediterranean. Yet contrary to their grim expectations, the aftermath had remained eerily quiet. Within six months, the relentless paranoia subsided, and the crew settled into a languid, comfortable rhythm in their coastal retreat.

Now, nearly a full year had passed since the contract. Wang Ryun had flown out to Tokyo the previous week on private business, leaving the villa pleasantly quiet.

Jakyeong had originally intended to use his massive windfall to purchase a private island, but the prime real estate carried extortionate maintenance fees, while the affordable plots suffered from glaring infrastructural flaws. He remained caught in a state of indefinite deliberation.

Wang Han, meanwhile, had finally undergone his long-awaited hair transplant procedure. The clinical results were surprisingly miraculous, leaving him with a full, thick hairline. Watching the lethal syndicate veteran tenderly wash his scalp with the hyper-delicate care reserved for a newborn infant never failed to make Jakyeong burst into laughter.

"Awake at last?" Wang Han called out, waving a pair of barbecue tongs. "Come grab a skewer."

Jakyeong gave a lazy wave of his hand, drifting toward the garden path. Eating heavily spiced meat the second he rolled out of bed held zero appeal.

Instead, he drew a cigarette from his pocket, sparking the tip.

Before the smoke could clear, Sasha came bounding across the turf, her sundress fluttering in the warm breeze. She thrust a freshly grilled skewer toward his chest with a bright grin.

"Here."

Unable to decline the sweet gesture, Jakyeong accepted the skewer. "Thank you."

She fell into step beside him, chattering away in rapid, melodic Russian. Dressed with twin braided pigtails that reached his shoulders, she possessed large, curious blue eyes and deep, endearing dimples that indented her cheeks whenever she smiled.

Jakyeong understood roughly half of her words, filling in the blanks through context and nodding along with an easy smile.

Pausing before a blossoming plumeria tree, she stretched her arms toward a high branch, trying to pluck a pristine ivory blossom. When her fingertips fell inches short, she turned an expectant, pleading look toward Jakyeong.

Smiling, Jakyeong reached up, snapped the stem cleanly, and handed the flower over.

Sasha beamed, offering the blossom back while tapping the side of her temple, silently requesting that he tuck it behind her ear. Jakyeong chuckled, gently securing the petals into her hair.

She tilted her head, asking if she looked pretty.

"Yes. Very pretty."

Her radiant, unvarnished grin was undeniably lovely.

Before Jakyeong could react, her small hand reached up, plucking the lit cigarette straight from his lips and placing it between her own with an impish wink.

From across the lawn, Wang Han let out a low, teasing whistle. Catching the suggestive smirk on Han's face, Jakyeong shot him an annoyed scowl, tossing the finished skewer into the disposal and wandering deeper into the garden.

Jakyeong spent the humid afternoon reclining in a canvas hammock slung between two broad palms.

The sunny skies gave way to an afternoon downpour, heavy raindrops drumming a steady, rhythmic cadence against the broad tropical foliage. Lying cocooned in the fabric, Jakyeong surrendered entirely to the soothing, drowsy warmth of the summer rain.

Having stuffed himself with roasted meats and beer before taking a lengthy midday nap, Wang Han finally emerged onto the veranda, lazily scratching his shoulder. He dragged a teak chair over, settling beside the hammock and sparking a cigarette.

Yawning widely toward the falling rain, Han blew a thick ring of smoke into the damp air.

"Don't you think it's about time we picked up a fresh contract?"

After months of absolute leisure, the quiet itch of restlessness was catching up to Jakyeong as well. He had amassed a staggering fortune, but living entirely off reserves wasn't sustainable in the long run.

"Dmitri reached out again," Han noted quietly. "He's drowning in high-end contracts, but he lacks an operative with your specific caliber. Finding someone who matches your efficiency is nearly impossible."

"No," Jakyeong replied flatly. "I will never take another job through that bastard."

Han nodded in silent understanding, letting the matter drop. Dmitri's covert switch of clients in Seoul had compromised their operational security, nearly getting Jakyeong butchered under Kang Il-hyun's thumb.

Since fleeing Korean waters, Jakyeong had never once searched for news regarding Kang Il-hyun. Whenever Han or Ryun inquired about the aftermath, he deflected with total indifference.

He refused to let his mind wander toward that man. He knew deep down that the tangled knot in his chest wasn't purely forged from hatred or revulsion—and that very realization made him refuse to acknowledge it all the more.

He closed his eyes, letting the heavy drumming of the tropical rain wash over his senses.

The thick, humid air carried the rich aroma of Han's tobacco. Finished with his smoke, Han reached out, gently rocking the canvas hammock from side to side.

"You look just like an infant in a cradle," Han chuckled.

Jakyeong let out a soft laugh. "Don't be ridiculous."

"Remember when you were little and I used to rock you to sleep like this?"

"Liar. I was ten years old when we met."

"You were so malnourished you were the size of a toddler."

Jakyeong smiled, letting the gentle sway coax him deeper into relaxation.

Wang Han began humming a low, wordless melody beneath his breath. The deep, soothing baritone blended seamlessly with the patter of the rain, wrapping the garden in absolute serenity.

Even long after Han had stubbed his smoke and retreated inside, Jakyeong remained nestled in the hammock, listening to the rain fall against the leaves.

It was an afternoon of absolute, unblemished peace.
